resources.string: See the apps %1$s’s phones reported and the rule for each.
The app list could not be loaded. This is not an empty list. Check the connection or try again.
App control is off for this child, so there is no app list.
Rules apply to %1$s on all of %1$s’s phones.
%1$s’s phones haven’t sent their apps. Other rules still apply.
No reported app matches. Apps that are not reported yet cannot appear here.
Which apps are essential is decided on each phone, so the list can differ between %1$s’s phones. They can’t be blocked or limited.
%1$s hasn’t sent its app list yet. Its apps may be missing here.
%1$s hasn’t sent its app list since %2$s. Apps installed since then may be missing here.
%1$s sent %2$d of %3$d apps. Some apps may be missing here.
Needed for the phone to work, so it is always allowed for %1$s.
%1$s can’t open it. Extra time can’t unblock it.
Never paused by %1$s’s limits or Downtime and not counted.
Its own limit inside %1$s’s daily limit. Downtime still applies.
Paused until a parent allows it. Approve it under Requests when %1$s asks.
Counts toward %1$s’s daily limit and follows Downtime.
No current phone reported this app. The rule is still saved on the router.
Draft changes do not cancel an unresolved save.
Current router policy matches. This does not prove who saved it.
Save refused before commit. No change from this attempt.
Policy changed. Review the current rule before saving a new draft. The earlier outcome is not a receipt.
The original operation expired and current policy does not match. Review before a new save.
Outcome unknown. Check status before any retry. The original operation is retained.
The base revision matches. You may retry the original signed operation.
Saved policy is not a phone acknowledgement. Offline phones receive changes at their next successful sync; no received or applied time is known here.
Rule editing is unavailable until an administrator explicitly activates core configuration in router administration. Nothing was imported by this attempt.
Save was not sent. Check the connection and current child scope, then try again.
